title: Image / Camera heading
narration: This section is where you choose the photograph you want to analyze. Select Choose Image to load a picture of the table. For a new camera photo, return to the pool-table screen and use the camera button beside Image Camera. Include the whole playing surface and use a clear, evenly lit image.

title: Table Setup heading
narration: Table Setup turns your photograph into a usable ball layout. Start with Auto Corners and check the table alignment. Choose the rack type, then select Analyze Balls. Review the detected balls, add any missed balls, and correct their identities before applying the layout.

title: Reset Corners
narration: Reset Corners clears the table reference points and detected balls so you can align the photograph again. Move the crosshair to each inside playing-surface corner and click in order: top left, top right, bottom right, then bottom left. Analyze the balls again after the alignment is correct.

title: AI detection mode
narration: The AI button enables or disables the trained ball detector. Ready means the models are loaded. Auto or Loading means they are preparing. Retry restarts a failed load. With AI off, Analyze Balls uses the original detector. Review the detected identities and positions before applying your layout.

title: Saved Images dropdown
control: Analyze: photoArchiveSelect and SAVED IMAGES heading
narration: Saved Images lists the photographs saved inside this app on this device. Choose the photograph you want to work with, then select Open. Choosing an entry in the list does not open it by itself.

title: Open saved image
narration: Open loads the photograph selected in Saved Images into the analysis workspace. Check the table corners and analyze the balls again. Saved Images stores the photograph; a saved trainer layout is kept separately.

title: Remove saved image
narration: Remove deletes the selected photograph from the app’s saved images on this device. The button changes to Confirm Remove. Press it again to complete the removal. Copies you already downloaded remain on your device.

title: Save current image
narration: Save keeps the current photograph inside the app on this device so you can open it again from Saved Images. The button shows Saved when the image is already stored. To save the reviewed ball arrangement as a trainer layout, use Apply and Save Layout instead.

title: Download current image
narration: Download saves a JPEG copy of the current source photograph to your device. This gives you a separate image file you can keep or share. It does not save the detected ball arrangement as a trainer layout.

title: Layout name
narration: Enter a descriptive name for the reviewed ball arrangement, then choose Apply and Save Layout. Use a name that helps you recognize the practice situation later, such as a bank-shot setup or a three-ball runout.

title: Explorer launcher
narration: Explorer is your tour of the trainer’s controls and layout. Turn it on, point to a button, field, ball, or visual reference, then click or tap to hear its explanation. While Explorer is on, those actions explain the feature without changing your setup. Turn Explorer off to use the controls normally.

title: Guide launcher
narration: Guide contains techniques, practice ideas, drills, and exercises. Choose a category and lesson, then press Play. Read shows the lesson’s narration. The trainer controls remain available while you study. For a tour of what each control does, use the separate Explorer button.

title: Get Started launcher
narration: Get Started opens the introductory lesson list. Begin with the first lesson or choose the topic you need. The lessons introduce your first aiming adjustments, shot execution, and practice sequence. Use the A button if you want the next lesson to play automatically.

title: Autoplay A
narration: The A button turns autoplay on or off. Green means on, and gray means off. With autoplay on, the next lesson in the current category and skill-level list starts after the current lesson finishes. Playback stops at the end of that list. Select a lesson and press Play to begin.

title: Close Analyze
narration: The X closes the analysis workspace and returns you to the pool-table screen. To transfer your reviewed ball arrangement before leaving, select Apply to Trainer Table. Use Apply and Save Layout if you also want to keep that arrangement for future practice.

title: Learning at your own pace
narration: You do not need to complete every lesson before using the trainer. Use Explorer when you want to learn a control. Open Guide for techniques and practice ideas. Experiment with shots and return to any lesson whenever it helps.

title: Understanding controls
narration: When you are unsure what a control does, turn on Explorer. Point to the control and click or tap to hear its explanation. Turn Explorer off when you are ready to adjust the control and try it yourself.

title: Understanding visual references
narration: The trainer displays visual references for aiming, ball contact, and cue-ball movement. Turn on Explorer and click a reference to learn what it represents. Use Guide for lessons that show how to apply those ideas in practice.

title: Help for a specific feature
narration: Explorer explains the feature you click, whether it is a shot-speed control, tangent line, or layout tool. Guide provides the related techniques, drills, and exercises. Choose the tool that matches what you want to learn.

title: Skill level
control: Both players: skill-level slider; replace guide-learning-level-quick
narration: The skill-level slider changes which lessons are available. Begin at Beginner for the introductory explanations. Move to Intermediate or Advanced to include more detailed lessons. Choose a lesson from the updated list and study it at your own pace.

title: Playback controls
control: Both players: Stop, Play/Pause, Back, Forward; replace guide-playback-controls-quick
narration: Play starts the selected lesson, and Pause holds your place. Stop returns the lesson to its beginning. Back and Forward move ten seconds through the recording. The A button turns automatic playback of the next lesson on or off. Read displays the narration text.

title: Pick and Play Full Racks
status: script-ready; MP3 not generated; device speech fallback
narration: Pick and Play Full Racks prepares a complete game rack. Choose 3-Ball, 6-Ball, 7-Ball, 8-Ball, 9-Ball, 10-Ball, Ultimate 8 Ball, or Straight Pool from the menu, then press Start. Six Ball uses a small triangle. Seven Ball places the seven in the center of a hexagon. Straight Pool prepares fourteen balls with the front position open. Add a single ball if you want a separate break ball, then drag it and the cue ball to your preferred positions. Ultimate 8 Ball uses the fixed numbered arrangement and puts the eight ball exactly on the foot spot.

title: Start selected full rack
status: script-ready; MP3 not generated; device speech fallback
narration: Start replaces the current table with the selected full rack and begins a fresh practice run. It prepares the selected rack, including the fourteen-ball straight-pool rack with its front position open. Use Execute Shot when you are ready to shoot.

title: Choose random ball count
status: script-ready; MP3 not generated; device speech fallback
narration: Choose how many numbered object balls to place randomly, then press Add Groups of Balls. Full racks are available separately in Pick and Play Full Racks.

title: Practice pathway
narration: Start with cue ball speed and contact, then target landing, pattern play, and kick routes. Finish with a scored benchmark. Open More for the matching video. Watch the creator demonstrate the layout, then build your own practice table. Save a starting layout before changing it so you can repeat the same test. Count pocketing, cue ball position, and legal contact separately. Your score should show what improved and what still needs work.

title: Speed and contact baseline
narration: Begin with a straight shot and center cue tip contact. Find the speed that produces a stop shot, then move the contact point higher for follow and lower for draw. Keep the object ball and pocket fixed while changing one setting at a time. Next, use a cut shot to compare the tangent line with the cue ball route. Before each shot, name the landing point you expect. Repeat each setup five times and record whether the cue ball finished short, long, left, or right.

title: Target landing precision
control: Main Guide > drills > Cue Ball Control
narration: Set up a repeatable object ball shot and choose a small cue ball landing zone. Begin with a generous target, then reduce it as your control improves. For this practice plan, use a three inch target and count a success only when the object ball is pocketed and the cue ball center finishes inside the target. Shoot ten attempts. Change only speed, then contact height, then the cut angle. Aim for eight successes out of ten before making the target smaller. Open More for Dr. Dave’s target practice demonstration.

title: Rock Around the Clock
narration: Open More and use Niels Feijen’s demonstration to set up Rock Around the Clock. Save the starting layout. Before every shot, choose the next object ball, its pocket, and the cue ball landing zone that leaves a useful angle. Prefer a route with room for a small speed error. Track pocketing and position separately. Complete one rotation first, then work toward three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball. When you miss position, repeat the previous shot and compare a simpler route before changing the whole pattern.

title: One-rail kick reference
narration: Place an object ball behind a blocker so the cue ball needs one cushion to reach it. Open More for the diamond system tutorial. Identify the cue ball start, the rail aim point, and the intended object ball contact. Keep speed and spin consistent while testing the route. Repeat five attempts, moving the rail aim point by a small amount when the contact misses. Record the adjustment that works, then test a second starting location. Count legal object ball contact according to the game you are practicing.

title: Two-rail kick extension
narration: Begin with a two cushion route that has space for the cue ball to travel. Mark the first rail aim point and predict the second rail contact before shooting. Keep the same speed and spin for each attempt. If the first contact is wrong, adjust the aim point. If the first contact is right but the final contact misses, examine the second rail route and speed. Record five attempts from the same start, then move the cue ball to a new starting diamond. Open More for the linked kick reference.

title: Corner-5 three-rail route
narration: Open More for Dr. Dave’s Corner-5 demonstration. Follow its starting, aiming, and arrival number scales together. Identify all three cushion contacts before you shoot. Start with a clear route, consistent speed, and the spin shown in the lesson. Compare the predicted arrival with the actual arrival, then make a small adjustment and repeat. Once the route is calibrated, add a target object ball and a blocker for escape practice. Test five different starting positions and record legal object ball contact separately from the final cue ball position.

title: Progressive difficulty benchmark
narration: Open More for Sharivari’s progressive difficulty drill and use the demonstrated setup. Save the starting layout and record your first score. For your Trainer adaptation, begin with a comfortable position zone. After a successful set, reduce the zone or increase the shot difficulty, changing one condition at a time. Count both the pocketed ball and the required cue ball position. If the same error repeats, return to the last successful level. Record the highest level you can repeat, rather than only your best isolated attempt.

title: 105-minute practice session
narration: Use this one hundred and five minute practice plan. Spend thirty minutes on speed and target landing, aiming for eight successful pocket and position results out of ten with a three inch target. Spend forty five minutes on Rock Around the Clock, first completing one rotation and then working toward three consecutive rotations without disturbing another ball. Spend thirty minutes on kick escapes, starting with one rail and adding two and three rails as control improves. Test five selected escapes and aim for four legal contacts. Record the result at the end of each phase. If time runs out, save your layout and score, then continue there next session.

title: Review, save, and repeat
narration: At the end of practice, record attempts, pocketed balls, successful position results, and legal kick contacts. Note the most common miss and the single adjustment that helped. Save the table with a name that includes the drill, difficulty, and date. Download its table file if you want to share the same layout with an instructor or student. Begin your next session with that saved layout and the same scoring conditions. Improve the weakest result first, then increase the challenge once you can repeat the improvement.
